_meta.rules: Sentence case. Say what happens, not feature names. No exclamation marks. {brand} is the operator's name; {sender} is the sender's display name or 'Someone'. Plurals use ICU syntax.

send.title: Send a secret
send.placeholder: Type or paste a password, a login, a private note…
send.title_hint: Shown to them before they open it.
send.detected: Found {count, plural, one {# field} other {# fields}} in your paste
send.keep_open: Keep this page open until it’s done. If your connection drops, it picks up where it stopped.
send.error_offline: Couldn’t connect to {host}. Nothing was sent, and what you typed is still here.
send.retry_note: Trying again won’t send anything twice.
send.editor_sub: Only the person with the link can read it
send.empty_error: Type or paste something to send, or attach a file.
send.max_files: Up to {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} per link.
send.share_hint: Paste it into a chat or email to the person you’re sending it to.
send.lede_once: Only the person you send the link to can read it, and it deletes itself once it’s opened.
send.lede_until_expiry: Only the people you send the link to can read it, until it expires.
send.passphrase_tell: Send it separately, not with the link.
send.saved_locally: Your account couldn’t save this link, so it’s kept in this browser only.
send.not_saved: This link couldn’t be saved to Your links. Copy it now: this page is the only place it’s shown.

policy.passphrase_help: They type it to open the link. Tell it to them another way, like on a call.
policy.passphrase_empty: Enter a passphrase, or turn it off.

policy.destroy_after_on: It opens once, then it’s deleted for good.
policy.destroy_after_off: Anyone with the link can open it, as often as they like, until it expires.
policy.passphrase_generated: 20 random characters: practically impossible to guess.

dialog.qr_title: Scan to open on a phone
dialog.qr_note: The code is the whole link, so keep it just as private. Scanning it shows nothing until they press Reveal.

links.title: Your links

links.lede_local: Everything you sent or asked for from this browser, and its status.
links.empty_body: Send a secret and you’ll see it here with its status. You can destroy it early.
links.other_device_sub: No title or copy of the link in your account
links.contents: {fields, plural, =0 {} one {# field} other {# fields}}{both, select, true {, } other {}}{files, plural, =0 {} one {# file} other {# files}}

links.empty_lede: Everything you send or ask for shows up here, with its status.
links.delete_body: It’s removed from Your links. This can’t be undone.
links.delete_body_live: The link stops working right away and it’s removed from Your links. This can’t be undone.
links.clear_body: They no longer work, and they’d leave on their own 30 days after expiring. This removes them from Your links now, and can’t be undone.
links.rename_help: Only you see this name. The person you sent it to still sees no title.
links.rename_help_title: Only you see this name. The person you sent it to still sees “{title}”.
links.note_account: End-to-end encrypted in your account. Only you can read these titles and links, on any device you sign in on.
links.note_local_signin: Saved in this browser only. Sign in to keep your links on every device.
links.note_demo: In the demo, links are saved in this browser only. On your own Cryptex, people sign in and their links are kept end-to-end encrypted on the server, on every device.
links.load_failed: Your links couldn’t be loaded. Nothing was changed.
links.delete_body_request: Its link stops working right away, an answer it has is destroyed, and it’s removed from Your links. This can’t be undone.

receipt.missing_body: It isn’t in Your links on this browser.

ask.title: Ask for a secret
ask.lede: Make a link and send it to someone. What they put in it is encrypted for you, and only you can open it.
ask.expires_help: The link and its answer expire together.
ask.share_hint: Send it to the person who has the secret. They don’t need an account, and they can answer once.
ask.unlock: Unlock your account first: the key that opens answers is kept there.
ask.local_note: Without an account, the answer opens only in this browser.
ask.note_help: Say who you are and what you need. Anyone with the link can read it.

answer.lede: Put it below. It’s encrypted on this device before it’s sent.
answer.answered_body: Each request takes one answer. If it wasn’t you who sent it, tell whoever asked.
answer.expired_body: Ask whoever sent it to you for a new link.
answer.closed_body: Whoever asked closed it. If they still need something, they’ll send a new link.
answer.title: Someone is asking you for a secret
answer.private: Encrypted on this device. Only the person who asked can open it, not even {host}.
answer.sent_body: It’s encrypted for the person who asked, and nobody else. You can close this page.
answer.passphrase_tell: Tell them the passphrase another way, like on a call. They need it to open what you sent.

reveal.contents: {fields, plural, =0 {} one {# field} other {# fields}}{both, select, true { and } other {}}{files, plural, =0 {} one {# file} other {# files}}
reveal.nothing_opened: It stays sealed until you press Reveal. Expecting something from {brand}? Check that the address is {host}.
reveal.passphrase_hint: {sender} should have given you the passphrase separately, for example on a call.
reveal.deleted_banner: The link no longer works. Save what you need before you leave this page.
reveal.clipboard_note: Copied values stay in your clipboard. Paste them into your password manager.
reveal.gone_opened_body: It could be opened only once. If that wasn’t you, someone else may have seen it.
reveal.gone_destroyed_body: It was deleted before anyone opened it.
reveal.broken_title: Part of this link is missing
reveal.unsupported: This page needs a newer browser. Update your browser, then open the link again.
reveal.opens_once_rich: {lead} After you reveal it, it’s gone for good.
reveal.nothing_opened_no_brand: It stays sealed until you press Reveal. Expecting something from this sender? Check that the address is {host}.
reveal.report_body: It’s deleted for everyone, now. Report links that look like phishing, malware or abuse.
reveal.broken_body_rich: Some apps cut long links short, and the missing end is needed to open it. {safe}
reveal.broken_fix_anon: Copy the whole link again, including everything after {hash}, or ask the sender to resend it.
reveal.cleared_deleted: It was deleted when you revealed it, and this page no longer shows it.
reveal.cleared_clipboard: Anything you copied is still in your clipboard. Paste it into your password manager, then clear it.
reveal.gone_expired_body_anon: It was never opened, and it’s been deleted. Ask the sender to send it again.
reveal.gone_tries_body: Someone entered the wrong passphrase too many times, so it was deleted before it could be read.
reveal.gone_tell_anon: Tell the sender so they can change the password and send a new link.
reveal.not_found_body: If someone sent you a link, it may be incomplete. Copy the whole link again, including everything after {hash}.
reveal.opens_until_expiry: Can be opened more than once, until it expires.
reveal.still_works_copy: The link keeps working until it expires. This page is your copy.
reveal.cleared_still_works: This page no longer shows it. The link still works until it expires.
reveal.gone_expired_body_opened: It was opened before it expired, and now it’s been deleted. Ask the sender if you need it again.
reveal.gone_destroyed_body_opened: The sender destroyed it after it had been opened. Ask them if you still need it.
reveal.gone_reported_body: Someone reported it as abuse, so it was deleted for everyone.
reveal.clear_soon: This page clears itself in under a minute, to keep the secret safe.
reveal.stopped_body: It was opened, but the download stopped before it finished. Try again to continue where it left off.
reveal.unfinished_body: It was opened here, but the download stopped and can’t be continued, and the link no longer works. Ask {sender} to send it again.
reveal.opened_here_title: You opened this link in this tab
reveal.opened_here_body: You revealed it here on {date}. Its key was removed from the address bar then, so this page can’t show it again. If the link can be opened more than once, open it again from the message you got.
reveal.opened_here_gone_body: You revealed it here on {date}, and it no longer works. If you didn’t save what you needed, ask the sender to send it again.
reveal.dropped_title: This link was most likely opened here
reveal.dropped_body: This tab asked to open it on {date}, but the connection dropped before the secret arrived. It counts as opened, so it can’t be opened again. Ask the sender to send it again.
reveal.gone_tries_body_opened: It had already been opened. Then someone entered the wrong passphrase too many times, so it was deleted.
reveal.passphrase_hint_anon: The sender should have given you the passphrase separately, for example on a call.

demo.self_host_body: No limits, your domain, your branding. The setup guide walks you through it.
demo.banner_marked: {lead} Links expire within an hour and everything is wiped nightly.

boot.insecure_body: Cryptex encrypts in your browser, and browsers allow that only on https:// pages (or at localhost on this computer). If you run this server, put it behind an HTTPS proxy.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: {brand} runs this Cryptex server at {host} so people can send secrets, such as passwords and files, through end-to-end encrypted links that expire.
privacy.cant_see_body: Secrets are encrypted in your browser before they’re uploaded. The key is in the part of the link after {hash}, which browsers don’t send to us. We can’t read what you send, its title, its file names or who it’s from, and neither can anyone who gets a copy of our database.
privacy.store_title: What we store, and for how long
privacy.row_secret_kept: Until it expires or is destroyed, or until it’s opened if it’s a one-time link
privacy.row_events: Events: links created, opened or destroyed, sign-ins and account changes. Never contents, titles or IP addresses
privacy.row_events_why: So senders can see what happened, and for security (the audit log)
privacy.row_events_kept: Set by the operator, 365 days by default
privacy.row_account: Your account, if you have one: username, role, when it was last used, and a verifier of your password (never the password itself)
privacy.row_account_why: To let you sign in and send, and to show your username to recipients who are signed in here too
privacy.row_cookie: A session cookie, if you sign in
privacy.row_cookie_kept: 14 days after your last visit, 30 days at most. On a shared computer, until the browser closes (12 hours at most).
privacy.no_tracking: There are no analytics, advertising or third-party scripts, and no cookies for people who only open links. Your IP address is used briefly to limit abuse and isn’t stored with secrets or in the audit log.
privacy.limit_title: A limit you should know about
privacy.limit_body: Like every web-based encryption tool, this one relies on the code this server sends to your browser. If you need protection even from the people running this server, run Cryptex on a server you control.
privacy.demo_body: Don’t send real secrets. Everything is deleted within an hour and the whole service is wiped every night.
privacy.lede_no_brand: This Cryptex server at {host} lets people send secrets, such as passwords and files, through end-to-end encrypted links that expire.
privacy.row_gone: A note that a link is gone, and why
privacy.row_gone_why: To tell whoever opens it later what happened
privacy.row_gone_kept: 30 days after the secret is gone
privacy.row_totp: Your 2FA secret, if you turn 2FA on (encrypted)
privacy.row_totp_kept: Until you turn 2FA off or your account is removed
privacy.row_vault: Your saved links, encrypted in your browser with a key we don’t have, and an encrypted key for each browser where you stay signed in (never on a shared computer)
privacy.row_vault_why: So you can see and manage them on every device
privacy.row_vault_kept: While your account exists; a browser’s key until you sign out there
privacy.row_temp: A temporary password or a reset link, if one is made for you
privacy.row_temp_kept: 24 hours at most, less if it’s used or your password changes

invite.incomplete: This invite link is incomplete. Copy the whole link, including everything after #.
invite.reset_lede: Your sign-in was reset. Choose a new password. You can add your authenticator app again too.
invite.joining: You’re joining {brand}’s secure share as {role, select, owner {an owner} other {a member}}. You’ll sign in as {username}
invite.joining_no_brand: You’re joining this server’s secure share as {role, select, owner {an owner} other {a member}}. You’ll sign in as {username}
invite.use_2fa_help: Recommended. You’ll sign in with your password and a code from an authenticator app.

totp.later: You can turn it on later under Your account, in the account menu.
totp.step_scan: Scan this QR code with an authenticator app
totp.apps: 1Password, Google Authenticator, Authy or any similar app.
totp.or_key: Can’t scan it? Enter this key in the app instead:

totp.step_add: Add Cryptex to your authenticator app
totp.or_copy: If nothing opens, copy this key into the app:

access.lede: Who can create links, and who has an account. Opening a link never needs one.
access.mode_help: Anyone can open the links people send.
access.anyone_help: Good on a private network. Rate limits still apply.
access.role_now: {name} is now {role, select, owner {an owner} other {a member}}
access.reset_body: They’ll get a link and a separate code. With both, they choose a new password and their 2FA is turned off; they can set it up again on the same page. Their current password keeps working until then, and they’re told about the link when they next sign in.
access.remove_body: They’re signed out and can’t sign in again. Links they already sent keep working until they expire.
access.password_help: At least 8 characters. Other devices are signed out.
access.password_changed: Password changed. Other devices were signed out.
access.totp_on_body: From now on, you’ll sign in with your password and a code from the app.
access.turn_off_body: Your password alone will sign in to this account.
access.lock_help: Their current password stops working and they’re signed out everywhere. Use this if the account may be in the wrong hands.

account.title: Your account
account.password_help: Changing it signs out your other devices.
account.totp_on_help: On. After your password, you enter a code from your authenticator app. New phone? Turn it off, then on again.
account.totp_off_help: Off. Your password alone signs you in. Turn it on for more protection.
account.demo_tour: This is a read-only tour. On your own server, each person manages their password and 2FA here.

reset.title: Reset your password
reset.lede: {by} made this link for {username}. It works once, until {date}. Enter the code {by} sent you separately, then choose a new password.
reset.code_help: 8 characters, like K7QP-2VR9. Case and dashes don’t matter.
reset.code_short: Enter all 8 characters of the code.
reset.totp_help: Your old 2FA is off. Set up an app now, or untick this and do it later under Your account.
reset.gone_body: It expired, was already used or cancelled, or the code was wrong too many times. Ask an owner for a new one.
reset.gone_tries_body: The code was entered wrong too many times, so this link stopped working. Ask an owner for a new one.
reset.links_note: Links you sent keep working and stay in Your links with their statuses. Their titles, and copies of links still waiting, are cleared. Requests you made are closed.

notice.title: Password reset link
notice.body: {by} made a link to reset your password on {date}. Your current password keeps working unless the link is used.
notice.ask_pending: Didn’t ask for it? Cancel the link, and tell another owner.
notice.ask_done: The link can’t be used any more. Didn’t ask for it? Tell another owner.

people.title: People
people.lede: Everyone signs in with a password, plus a code from an authenticator app if they turn on 2FA. Owners also manage this Server tab.
people.owner_help: Also manages this Server tab and its people.
people.member_help: Sends links and sees their own.
people.username_invalid: Use 2 to 32 letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or number. It’s what they sign in with.
people.invite_body: Send it to them yourself. It works once, until {date}, and lets them set a password and, if they want, an authenticator app. It’s shown only now.
people.invite_tip: Tip: send it as a one-time Cryptex link.
people.reset_ready_body: Send the link and the code by different channels, for example the link in chat and the code by phone, so neither alone is enough. They work once, until {date}, and are shown only now.

limits.lede: What people are offered when they send a secret.
limits.max_file_size_help: Per file. {free} of disk is free.
limits.errors: {n, plural, one {# change has an error} other {# changes have an error}}

branding.name_help: Shown next to your logo, with “{suffix}” after it.
branding.logo_help: Square SVG or PNG, at least 64 px.
branding.logo_type: Use an SVG or PNG file.
branding.logo_size: Use a file of {size} or less.
branding.preview_caption: What people see when they open a link from this server.

vault.adopt_title: Add links from this browser to your account?
vault.adopt_body: {n, plural, one {# link is} other {# links are}} kept in this browser only: sent before you signed in, or kept here because your account couldn’t save them. Add them to Your links on every device, or leave them in this browser only.
